bullets.title: PLTR Q2 Blowout: Revenue $1.94B, EPS $0.41, FY Guide Raised to $8.15-8.16B
bullets.body: Palantir smashed Q2 estimates across every metric—revenue $1.94B vs. $1.81B est., adj. EPS $0.41 vs. $0.35 est., adj. EBITDA $1.20B vs. $1.09B, US commercial revenue $764M vs. $716M. Full-year revenue guidance raised to $8.15-8.16B from $7.65-7.66B; Q3 guided at $2.16B vs. $2.0B expected. Rule of 40 score hit 155%. One analyst noted the 15% AH move was driven purely by a 14.4% EPS raise with the P/E multiple flat at ~59x—no re-rating, just earnings power.

bullets.title: NVDA: Huawei warns of physical chip limits; Rubin Ultra HBM despec is a supply issue, not demand
bullets.body: Huawei's top scientist warned NVDA and Western chipmakers are approaching physical limits of semiconductor scaling. Separately, a Seoul analyst note clarifies that Rubin Ultra's HBM downgrade from 12Hi to 8Hi is a supply constraint, not demand weakness—additional production will fill freed capacity. TrendForce also reports NVIDIA considering downgrading Rubin Ultra's HBM config due to DRAM shortage expected through 2027.

bullets.title: DRAM/HBM 2027 capacity fully sold out; customers receiving only 60-70% of requested volumes
bullets.body: Multiple sources (DigiTimes, Counterpoint) confirm SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung have sold out 2027 DRAM and HBM capacity ahead of schedule, with customers allocated only 60-70% of requested volumes. NAND flash bookings expected to be fully filled by year-end. Counterpoint Q2 data shows SK Hynix revenue-based DRAM share only ~1pp ahead of Micron, with HBM3E pricing dynamics driving the shift.

bullets.title: MU: Micron NY permit process challenged; 2027 capacity already allocated
bullets.body: A lawsuit challenges New York state's permit approval process for Micron's planned chip facility. Separately, multiple supply chain reports confirm Micron's 2027 annual production capacity is fully allocated per Digitimes, a structural tailwind for pricing.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos files to sell $4.07B in shares; AWS capacity spoken for through 2028; custom silicon hits $25B run rate
bullets.body: Bezos filed a Form 144 to sell up to 15M AMZN shares (~$4.07B) under a 10b5-1 plan, sending the stock down ~1.9% AH. AWS exec confirmed on Bloomberg that capacity is fully spoken for through 2027 into 2028, with demand significantly outstripping supply. Amazon's custom silicon business has reached a $25B annual run rate.

bullets.title: IREN secures MSFT and NVDA AI cloud deals covering 85% of $4B revenue target; BofA takes 5.8% stake
bullets.body: IREN landed multi-year AI cloud contracts with Microsoft and NVIDIA covering approximately 85% of its $4B+ annualized revenue target. Bank of America also acquired a 5.8% stake in IREN, sparking bullish speculation.

bullets.title: Hot Chips 2026 lineup: NVDA Rubin/Vera, AMD MI400, INTC Diamond Rapids all featured
bullets.body: Hot Chips 2026 conference will showcase next-generation architectures including NVIDIA's Rubin and Vera, AMD's MI400, and Intel's Diamond Rapids, alongside memory tutorials covering Samsung and SK Hynix HBM technologies and a dedicated HBF session.

bullets.title: HBF memory standard advances: SK Hynix/SanDisk unveil specs; Google and Tenstorrent join consortium
bullets.body: SK Hynix and SanDisk unveiled the industry's first HBF standard specifications at FMS 2026, six months after launching the consortium. Google and Tenstorrent have joined. HBF is positioned as a complement to HBM—not a replacement—targeting large model weight and KV Cache memory bottlenecks with a more cost/power-efficient near-compute layer.

bullets.title: ORCL: Default risk hits historic high, surpassing 2008 GFC; Oracle supplying 22.6% of China's AI compute
bullets.body: Oracle's CDS spread reached its highest level in company history, exceeding 2008 GFC levels. Separately, Oracle was reported to have been providing 22.6% of China's known AI computing power.

bullets.title: AAPL: India sales top $10B for first time; MacBook Air shortage from memory chip scarcity
bullets.body: Apple's annual sales in India exceeded $10B for the first time, signaling strong emerging market growth. Concurrently, Apple faces MacBook Air shortages driven by memory chip supply constraints, with supply chain disruption expected to ripple through partners.

bullets.title: AXTI and AAOI: Massive rebounds from lows on AI/data center optical demand
bullets.body: One fintwit account highlighted AXTI +98% and AAOI +57% from recent lows as top portfolio performers, citing InP substrate demand for lasers and CPO (AXTI) and optical transceiver strength for data centers (AAOI). AAOI is also up 12%+ on the session, breaking back above its 200-day EMA ahead of Thursday Q2 earnings.

bullets.title: TSMC: Kumamoto JASM fab returns to full operations; Sony JV in advanced stages
bullets.body: TSMC confirmed its Kumamoto JASM fab returned to full operations after prior disruptions. Separately, Sony is in advanced talks with TSMC for a joint venture image sensor production facility in Kumamoto, with Sony allocating ¥10B for the venture.

bullets.title: INTC: EMIB-T packaging costs 50% less than TSMC CoWoS; Trump cites Intel as government equity stake template
bullets.body: Reports indicate Intel's EMIB-T advanced packaging costs 50% less than TSMC CoWoS, with yields exceeding 90% and mass production starting next year. Separately, Trump has repeatedly cited the Intel deal as a template for government equity participation in strategically important companies as an alternative to direct subsidies.

bullets.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Max at aggressive $2/$6 per million token pricing; challenges U.S. AI rivals
bullets.body: Alibaba released its biggest-ever AI model, Qwen3.8-Max, built on 2.4T parameters, priced aggressively at $2/million input tokens and $6/million output tokens. Model weights will be released publicly next week. Internal testing shows the model can independently run software engineering projects over 16-day periods.

bullets.title: Macro: Biggest momentum drawdown since 2008 alongside record tech weekly inflows; S&P best month start since Oct 2022
bullets.body: Howard Lindzon flagged the biggest momentum drawdown since 2008 occurring simultaneously with the largest tech weekly inflows in history, with BofA issuing a bull/bear signal. S&P 500 rose 1.5% Monday in its best month start since October 2022, with megacaps posting their best day since March as Middle East tensions eased and oil fell 5%.

bullets.title: Japan margin trading at 1990 highs; $36.6B yen intervention spent Friday; U.S.-Japan intervention may not be durable
bullets.body: Margin trading in Japan reached its highest level since 1990—a level that preceded an 80%+ Nikkei decline over 18 years. Japan spent ~$36.58B buying yen in Friday's coordinated intervention, but WSJ and analysts note the intervention may not be sufficient to sustainably reverse the yen's slide.

bullets.title: SNAP Q2 beats across revenue, DAU, and EBITDA; Q3 EBITDA guidance misses midpoint
bullets.body: Snap reported Q2 revenue of $1.60B vs. $1.54B est., adj. EBITDA of $250M vs. $192M est., and DAU of 493M vs. 488M est. Q3 revenue guided to $1.70-1.74B (in-line), but Q3 adj. EBITDA of $300-350M missed the $330M consensus. CEO flagged AI reviewing 90% of code pull requests and AR Specs as the largest long-term opportunity with a Sept. 16 LA launch event.

bullets.title: MSFT: Trading above 200-day MA at widest margin since October; data center real estate is next bottleneck
bullets.body: Microsoft is trading above its 200-day moving average by the widest margin since October, a bullish technical signal. One fintwit account highlighted that MSFT's real constraint for AI/cloud expansion is not land but AI-ready real estate with sufficient power, cooling, and permits.

bullets.title: NVDA GPU prices surge 30% in China amid stockpiling fears; consumer chip demand accelerating
bullets.body: Consumer graphics card prices surged 30% in one week in China's Shenzhen wholesale market, with NVIDIA RTX 5060 among the biggest gainers. Buyers are stockpiling ahead of anticipated price increases, suggesting front-loaded demand that could affect near-term supply/demand dynamics.

bullets.title: SMH showing capitulation signal; July semi selloff driven by forced liquidation not fundamentals
bullets.body: SMH ETF recorded its highest single-day volume ever last Wednesday after a 25% pullback, with a close on the low suggesting classic capitulation selling. One analyst noted the July semiconductor selloff was caused by forced liquidation across the sector with no fundamental deterioration—a potential contrarian buy signal as retail investors were among the heaviest buyers of semis through July.
